analysis.name: Ahmed Alif
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My favorite class that I have taken in this program thusfar. It is clear that he truly cares about his students and our growth. I liked his incorporation of media, and found class discussions to be very interesting and practically applicable.

Prof. Alif is radically honest. He makes it clear what you need to do to improve. He's very data and research-oriented, using real frameworks and pushes you to apply them. He's also very responsive, and is flexible when life happens. The syllabus had some early revisions that were a bit confusing, but he addressed it and improved it.

Professor Alif's HBSE II is a thought-provoking class that pushes you to think beyond memorizing theories. He's passionate about social justice and encourages students to question systems and assumptions. The coursework can be challenging, but if you participate, do the readings, and stay open-minded, you'll get a lot out of the experience.

Professor Alif is a knowledgeable professor who expects students to stay engaged. Attendance is mandatory, and there is a required book with regular readings, so preparation matters. The syllabus may change to include new material, but it keeps the course relevant and challenging. If you show up ready to work, you can get a lot out of the class.

Professor Alif, is knowledgeable and insightful and uses mixed media to guide the class. He does change up the curriculum, I find it helps keep up with current events. He's cerebral and it translates in his teaching style, but you're learning from a clinician/scholar which is a plus. I'd his class again in a heart beat.

review_highlights.comment: Abel is amazing and one of my favorite professors at NYU. As others mentioned, he weighs out materials before class which saves a lot of time. His grading was pretty fair, and he was very helpful and supportive with a lot of questions I had (def go to his office hours btw). Orgo lab is difficult but I enjoyed it and learned a lot from Abel.

Dr. Navarro is one of the most experienced TAs in the organic chemistry lab. He helped tremendously by measuring out compounds and setting up for us while the lab lecture was going on. If you are unsure about why you received a certain grade on the postlabs, it's very easy to get feedback from him which helps to improve in the class.

He is a very nice guy. Always helps you set up your stuff and answers your questions very nicely. But he is a VERY harsh grader. Very hard to get higher than an 80 on a lab report, even after checking it with a tutor beforehand. Also he just doesn't give 5/5 for safety ever, no matter what. But he is very very nice during the lab.

Upon taking organic chemistry this semester and finding out Abel had limited reviews, I was skeptical. Turns out, I could not have made a better decision. Not only can you relate to him on a personal basis, but he takes the time to help you understand the material. Grades are respectable when compared to the rest of the lab sections.

if you get him as a TA for orgo lab you're set. weighs out all the reagents for you so you don't have to stand and wait in the long line and you can get out earlier. very helpful and good at explaining concepts.

The best thing about him was definitely his vast knowledge of the topics of discussion. You could tell from the get-go that this man is a significant source of information on everything covered in the curriculum. However, the lectures are extremely boring and difficult to follow if you don't keep up with the readings.

Took Zweig for Modern Israel and absolutely loved it. Even though I'm not Jewish, I found the course incredibly relevant and manageable. His lectures are well-structured and interesting. He does a great job teaching multiple perspectives on the controversial history. He also offers lots of extra credit opportunity!

He definitely knows what he's talking about, however his lectures often linger on without engaging the students in discussion. He is clear when it comes to assignements and a fair grader, and overall a great guy but when it comes to lectures make sure you drink some caffeine before you attend.
